newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Heavy civilian death toll in Zaire fighting.
newsitem.headline: Heavy civilian death toll in Zaire fighting.

text.p: About 200 civilians and more than 100 soldiers from both sides of Zaire's civil war were killed in fighting around the town of Kenge, east of the capital Kinshasa, residents and other sources said on Wednesday.
The Zairean Red Cross said 10 of its workers were among those killed in the fighting on Tuesday, but would not elaborate on the other casualties.
"We've been in radio contact with Kenge via Bandundu. They confirm the death of 10 of our volunteers and have given us the names of the dead," a Zaire Red Cross official in Kinshasa told Reuters.

Other humanitarian sources in contact with Kenge put the civilian death toll at around 200 but they could not say how the civilians, including the Red Cross workers, were killed. "There were around 200 civilians killed at Kenge on Tuesday alone. We do not know yet how they were killed," one said.
The same source gave the death figure for the fighters as 100 on the government side and 15 for the rebels. A combined 126 were wounded, the source said.
Kenge, 250 km (150 miles) east of Kinshasa, is the nearest frontline town to capital, which is targeted by rebels closing in after seizing most of Zaire's territory in a seven-month offensive.
